# Deliver the first dependable-portions increment

Act as delivery coordinator for this repository. Read AGENT.md and its loading
rules, then the accepted release baseline in
[canonical-ingredient-correction/proposal.md](../../openspec/changes/canonical-ingredient-correction/proposal.md),
the selected owner tasks, and their immediate dependencies. Use the installed
OpenSpec apply workflow. This prompt selects the implementation increment below;
it is not an instruction to implement every active change.

## Outcome and accepted decisions

Build on existing locally qualified URL/photo intake and manual correction. Finish
the missing ordinary ingredient-to-step relationship path so a recipe can be
imported, edited, scaled and cooked with consistent supported quantities and one
ingredient-derived grocery demand. Do not rebuild the existing exact arithmetic,
guarded editor, projection engine, grocery checks or qualified photo publication.

- Automatic relationship maintenance applies both to import and saved ingredient
  or step edits. Reuse deterministic revalidation; an AI task in the existing
  workflow system may propose relationships when needed.
- The server validates association, numeric role, source evidence and current
  revisions. AI confidence or a `validated` label is not proof. Task 0.1 defines
  the bounded evidence inlet; do not substitute assumptions for this engineering work.
- AI reevaluation changes relationships only, never saved ingredient descriptions,
  quantities, units or instruction wording. Preserve human edits and explicit clears.
- No special markup or manual linking screen. Uncertain relationships retain original
  readable wording. Reads, projection and grocery recomputation make no AI calls.
- Retain supported whole/absolute/fraction/remainder/fixed/per-item behavior. Start
  with one whole-use tracer; do not call that completion of all supported forms.
- Frontend, backend and database deploy together. Older tabs refresh and reconcile
  recoverable drafts. No permanent legacy-string write adapter for canonical records.
- Planned maintenance is accepted. Reuse existing demo/online-recovery coordination
  with migration's data/draft preservation policy. Do not perform a demo reset or
  invent a parallel maintenance system. Deployment/restart rehearsal is separate
  from existing lease/reset tests.
- Bilingual catalogue/merging and Similar UI are deferred. Preserve existing fallback
  behavior and any references already persisted. Selective ingredient repair is superseded.
- PDF, synthesis, shared-recipe intake and general protected reimport are later
  bounded increments. Preserve their existing behavior and publication fences now.

## Establish the live starting point

Inspect status, HEAD, current selected tasks, source and exact evidence records.
The baseline recorded URL/photo at a666a64f; verify any newer work before assigning
it. Distinguish implementation from qualification. Do not rerun broad suites solely
because of a handoff. Do not trust a task count, historical prose or a worker's
success message as proof of current behavior.

Preserve unrelated dirty and staged files. Do not stash/reset another writer's
work to run hooks. Use isolated worktrees/checkouts where needed and coordinate
ports, databases, build outputs and CPU-intensive gates. Before starting, identify
any active owners and explicitly hand off shared paths.

## Orchestrate up to three workers

Use actual host capabilities; proceed sequentially if subagents are unavailable.
Workers may communicate directly about interface needs. The coordinator maintains
one dependency queue and one writer per shared file, resolves scope and integrates
results. Give each assignment its task IDs, concrete outcome, owned paths,
prerequisites, required checks and stopping point.

1. **B — critical path, relationship producer:** step change tasks 0.1–0.3. First
   define and exercise evidence validation; then implement one ordinary import/edit
   workflow tracer and extend the acceptance to affected supported roles. Own binding
   validation/projection/Cook code and relevant tests. Never infer proof from a
   seeded fixture or silently rewrite user content.
2. **A — canonical integration:** canonical tasks 2.1–2.2 and 3.2, bounded to B's
   accepted Save/publication hooks and the first increment. Own CanonicalRecipeContentStore,
   RecipeService and RecipeFilePublicationStore changes. Reuse qualified URL/photo
   paths; do not start later intake channels. Preserve source/revision/protection,
   draft recovery, stale-result rejection and one-demand behavior.
3. **C — independent migration preparation:** migration tasks 1.1 and the read-only
   assessment portion of 3.1. Produce/reconcile the no-write inventory and concrete
   existing-recovery reuse plan on disposable copies. Do not activate conversion,
   modify shared publication code concurrently, or invent a new recovery API.
   Report the dependency on final persisted bindings for later recovery acceptance.

The coordinator owns integration, current OpenSpec task bookkeeping and assignment
of shared OpenAPI/generated-client/mock/CI edits. If an interface changes, synchronize
its real consumers and method-sensitive mocks in the same vertical slice. Don't
create independent backend/frontend batches that integrate only at the end.

## Acceptance and delivery rhythm

Complete one working path before widening it:

URL/photo import → saved canonical facts → ingredient edit → validated relationship
maintenance → step edit → optional workflow reevaluation → one coherent projection
at changed portions → explicit active-Cook refresh → one grocery demand.

Use real API/workflow/PostgreSQL and generated-client/browser seams; double external
providers only. Include ambiguous/repeated/Unicode spans, unrelated numbers, explicit
clears, unchanged/unrelated edits, stale completion after another edit, duplicate
delivery, provider failure and retained cooking state. Reuse existing allocation,
prepared/count and grocery baseline tests. Add meaningful red tests before missing
logic; don't manufacture red for already-correct behavior or weaken an oracle.

Workers run focused feedback using Taskfile owners. The coordinator reviews code,
contracts, test selection and exact result files, then runs applicable preparation
and one combined verification boundary on stable integrated source. Required live/
database cases have zero required skips. Report source/build/configuration identity,
first-attempt results, retries, failures, blocked and never-run stages separately.
Local success is not hosted success; preserve any required hosted gate as outstanding
unless it actually runs on the exact candidate.

## Completion and stopping boundary

Update the existing owner task records with implementation state, scenario coverage,
next action and evidence identity. Close a checkbox only when all its criteria pass.
Do not archive, synchronize main specs or claim the whole feature is done from this
increment. Do not deploy, mutate production/DV, push, merge or commit without separate
session authorization. Keep the changes reviewable and preserve unrelated work.

Finish with: delivered user behavior, remaining blockers, exact passed/failed/
blocked/not-run checks, changed paths and the next bounded assignment. Do not ask
again about accepted product decisions or routine engineering choices. Ask one
question only if a newly discovered consequential ambiguity cannot be resolved
from the accepted specs; keep independent work moving while it is pending.

Once selected, treat `--store <id>` as sticky for the rest of the workflow. Every unscoped example of those commands below is shorthand: before running it, append the flag. For example, run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json --store "<id>"`, not the unscoped form shown below. Other commands do not take the flag. Hints printed by commands already carry the flag; keep it on follow-ups. Without a store, commands act on the nearest local `openspec/` root.

**Project check:** These steps expect a project that already uses OpenSpec. Before the first step that writes anything (`new change`, `archive`, `sync specs`, or authoring an artifact file), confirm the project has a root: run `openspec list --json` (with `--store <id>` when a store is selected, since the store is then the root) and read `root`. A root object means the project is set up. `"root": null` means it is not - there is no `openspec/` directory here, and a write such as `openspec new change` would create one as a side effect. The command also exits non-zero, which is that answer rather than a broken CLI, so read the JSON instead of retrying or working around it.

One `"root": null` is not about setup: when a `status` error message starts with `Declared in` or `Invalid store declaration in` and names this project's `openspec/config.yaml` (or `config.yml`), the project does use OpenSpec through a store it declares, which this machine cannot resolve (the store is not registered, or the `store:` line is malformed). Otherwise, with no root, what happens next depends on how this workflow was reached:

- **Auto-selected**: you chose this workflow yourself, without the user naming OpenSpec, naming this skill, or running its slash command. # Contract and Testing Governance

## 1. Contract authority
- **OpenAPI is Law**: The `specs/openapi.yaml` is the ultimate source of truth.
- **Development sequence**: Approved contract/spec → tests → implementation.
- **API changes**: Update `specs/openapi.yaml` for every API change, including
  operations, payloads, status codes and observable behavior, before implementing
  the changed API. Regenerate the Kiota client with `task gen:client` (or scoped
  `task prepare`), then update affected consumers and schema-compliant mocks in
  the same slice. Use generated SDK types; do not hand-edit generated output.
- Resolve mismatches against approved intent. A failing test or divergent implementation
  does not authorize rewriting the contract to match code; obtain authorization for
  a changed contract when it exceeds the selected scope.

## 2. Test-first expectations
- **Test-Driven Development**: You must write or update tests before implementing logic.
- For bug fixes, add or update a regression test that reproduces the reported
  failure before implementation, and retain it after the fix.

Assert observable behavior, domain invariants and relevant side effects rather than
incidental implementation structure; retain tests for explicit architectural contracts.
For state-changing work, include relevant duplicate, retry, interruption and
unknown-outcome cases. A hand-verified representative example can seed these tests;
it does not replace real seam or database acceptance.

For each behavior increment, follow **red → green → refactor**:

1. **Red**: Write or update the smallest meaningful behavior test, run it before
   changing production logic, and observe failure for the intended missing or
   incorrect behavior. Compilation, tooling and service failures do not establish
   red. If the test already passes, establish the missing behavior before proceeding.
2. **Green**: Implement only enough of the selected behavior to make that test
   pass, then run it and the affected integration checks.
3. **Refactor**: Improve the implementation and tests where needed within the
   selected scope while keeping the checks green; rerun affected checks after edits.

Record the red and green commands/results in task evidence. Tests added only after
production logic do not satisfy TDD. Documentation-only changes have no behavior
cycle; identify that as not-applicable rather than inventing tests.

Use the approved behavior to judge a failing test. Determine whether the failure
is a regression, an expectation made stale by the authorized change, or a tooling
or environment problem before changing code. Update stale expectations to the
approved behavior; fix actual regressions. A test failure alone does not justify
undoing an authorized behavior change or weakening a valid test to obtain green.

When work spans sessions, preserve the approved behavior, changed paths, observed
red/green evidence and unresolved failures in the selected task or a meaningful
handoff. On resumption, reconcile that checkpoint with current code and tests
before editing. An unfinished TDD cycle is a checkpoint, not evidence that the
intended behavior should be reverted. Follow higher-priority host testing rules
where they constrain this procedure; report any resulting gap explicitly.

## 2a. Tracer bullets and vertical slices

Start implementation with a **tracer bullet**: the smallest working path through
all layers required by one observable scenario. For a browser/API capability,
connect UI → generated Kiota client → API → domain/service → persistence or workflow
where affected. Exercise the real internal seams and verify observable results and
side effects before widening the capability. Keep external-provider test doubles at
their boundaries; a mocked browser API alone does not prove backend integration.

Plan and complete one bounded vertical behavior slice at a time, each using the
red/green/refactor cycle and named integration acceptance checks. Do not implement
all backend, client or UI work in separate horizontal batches and defer integration
to the end. Include only layers the scenario actually needs; shared prerequisites
must serve the first working slice. Extend to additional scenarios only after that
path works, within the authorized task scope.

## 3. Drift prevention
- API request/response shapes must conform to OpenAPI. Internal domain and UI
  models may differ, with explicit mapping at API boundaries.
- **Schema Integrity**: Parity between the OpenAPI Specification, Mock API, and Backend implementation is mandatory.
- **Validation**: Run applicable checks selected by change class under [execution harness](execution-harness.md). Contract changes require affected seam and database behavior evidence; static checks alone cannot establish it.

## 4. Data and mock discipline
- **Mock implementation is part of every API change**: Add or update the affected
  method-sensitive handlers in `pwa/e2e/mock-api.ts`, plus supporting builders,
  fixtures and state transitions, in the same vertical slice as the real API.
  Match the approved contract's request/response shapes, status codes, errors and
  observable side effects, including subsequent reads and SSE where applicable.
  Updating types or fixtures alone is insufficient when handler behavior changes.
- **Mock acceptance**: Run tests that exercise the changed handlers and affected
  Playwright scenarios, including applicable success, failure and stateful behavior.
  Missing mock implementation or failing/blocked required mock checks prevents
  claiming the API change verified; static drift checks alone do not establish mock behavior.
- **Mock Standardization**: E2E mocks MUST use `MOCK_IDS` (valid GUIDs) and schema-compliant `builders`.
- **High-Fidelity Mocks**: Test factories (e.g., `TestWebApplicationFactory`) should prioritize mocks that preserve domain side-effects (e.g., persisting workflow instances to the DB) rather than "shallow" mocks that return empty success objects. This ensures vertical slice integration tests can verify system state correctly.

## 5. Definition of done
- The OpenAPI specification accurately reflects the required changes.
- Tests are written or updated before implementation code.
- Each behavior increment has observed red/green evidence and remains green after
  any refactoring. The tracer bullet and subsequent slices have passed their named
  integration acceptance checks across the affected layers.
- API changes include the updated OpenAPI contract, regenerated Kiota client,
  affected consumers, implemented mock handlers/builders/state behavior, passing
  mock acceptance checks and a passing `task gen:client:check`.
- Verify affected API/client seams with tests appropriate to the changed behavior.
  Name the required checks in the OpenSpec tasks.
- Applicable validation has actual command/results and tested content/config/runtime identity. Static route, DTO and mock-pattern checks establish only their inspected properties; live endpoint and database behavior evidence are separate.

Claim completion only when the selected scope's required acceptance and applicable
harness checks pass. Code existence or advisory guidance is not completion evidence;
a blocked required check prevents claiming completion.

## 6. Evidence and test scope

Classify each required check as passed, failed, blocked, not-run or not-applicable.
A failure calls for diagnosis: application defects, stale tests, infrastructure and
permissions are distinct possibilities. Logs and tests do not authorize changing
approved intent. Unknown impact takes conservative checks; mixed changes take the union. Git
differences and explicit path selection do not prove actor ownership. Preserve
unrelated work; include changes that overlap or alter a selected dependency/runtime
input in the verification review. Missing services,
interrupted checks and unqualified runners cannot become
passed evidence. Cache success belongs only to the actual tested identity.

Use testid-first interaction locators and semantic assertions for accessible role,
name, state and labeling. Preserve network isolation and schema-compliant builders.
For optimistic stores, assert both immediate UI state and reconciled server state.
Pure logic may move to unit tests within authorized scope, retaining E2E coverage of
navigation, network/state integration and user-visible behavior. Audits are advisory;
findings outside the selected task are evidence, not cleanup authorization.
# Execution harness

Use Taskfile.yml as the command interface. Inspect targets and scripts when their
effects or verification coverage are unclear. Commands do not grant authority to reset data, kill shared
processes, stage files or extend the selected task. A worktree alone does not isolate
processes, ports or databases.

## Preparation and verification

Before overlapping test or service work, coordinate ownership of ports, databases,
server processes, build outputs and output records, as well as shared CPU/memory
capacity. Prefer separating mutable state and using distinct task-owned resources
before serializing independent work. Serialize genuine dependencies or unavoidable
contention; keep one writer per shared file. A worktree is not runtime isolation.
Use snapshots or owned resources for focused feedback where supported and report

# Scale ingredient uses in cooking steps

> **Delivery baseline — 2026-11-10:** Baseline workstream B. Reuse the existing projection and Cook behavior; ordinary trusted binding production remains a required missing connection. The first whole-use tracer does not remove the other specified supported allocation forms. See the [release scope and agent coordination](../canonical-ingredient-correction/proposal.md#dependable-portions-delivery-baseline--accepted-2026-11-10).

## Why

Ingredient-only scaling leaves step quantities contradictory. Step uses need explicit revision-bound associations to original recipe demand while cooking remains available when a mapping is uncertain.

## Outcome and Scope

Mandatory ingredient-use scaling, coherent ingredient/step projection and current-recipe reading at recorded prepared counts. No general formula language, prose-wide numeric replacement or new grocery demand. Explicit partial amounts remain original after total correction and still scale with portions; relative language stays relative, with original readable wording for inconsistent allocations. Cook mode omits the routine step-uncertainty notice and duplicate header ingredients link; phone Edit/View Original actions return to the right while the view toggle stays left and tablet controls retain their lower-left layout.

## Implementation baseline and remaining delivery

The projection engine, original-step editor, coherent refresh, prepared-count consumers and Cook cleanup already exist. Existing unit, PostgreSQL and browser owners exercise whole, absolute, fraction, remainder, fixed and per-item behavior; their recorded results remain tied to their tested candidates. They are reusable implementation, not an instruction to build another engine.

The missing connection is ordinary trusted relationship production and maintenance through import and saved edits. Current conversion creates empty bindings and projection fixtures seed them. Group 0 in tasks.md owns that missing producer/validator and its real workflow acceptance. Groups 1–3 retain acceptance of supported behavior and identify only demonstrated gaps; group 4 and task 5.3 retain outstanding integration/release qualification. This change is not complete until ordinary URL/photo and manual-correction flows reach supported scaling without seeded relationships. Bilingual catalogue adoption and Similar-search UI are deferred from this release. Other intake expansion follows in later increments and is outside the first selected increment, not silently removed from the eventual requirements.

## What Changes

- Automatically maintain ingredient-to-step relationships during import and after saved ingredient or step edits, using the ordinary editor without special markup or mandatory manual linking. Reuse deterministic revalidation; allow a workflow AI task to propose replacements when necessary, subject to server evidence validation and stale-write protection. Uncertain text remains original and readable.
- **BREAKING:** adopt the applicable shared [contract](../canonical-ingredient-correction/contracts.md) with explicit compatibility/failure behavior.
- Preserve user decisions and existing safety boundaries in the shared [review](../canonical-ingredient-correction/review.md).
- Complete and reconcile adversarial acceptance from the shared [corpus](../canonical-ingredient-correction/acceptance-corpus.md); this consolidation changes planning artifacts only.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `cooking`: project validated uses and preserve cooking context.
- `supper-servings`: include step uses in shared portions projection.
- `recipe-editing`: guard instruction edits in original basis.

## Impact

Depends on the canonical foundation and companion ownership map as specified in design.md. Future apply must synchronize OpenAPI, generated clients, consumers and stateful mocks where affected, and qualify actual persistence/workflow seams. Planning existence does not establish implementation readiness.

name: dotnet-dev
description: Implement or fix WFS C# backend behavior, including controllers, services and persistence integration. Use for backend code changes, not frontend-only or specification-only work.
---

# WFS backend development

Use the selected behavior and [contract/testing](../../core/contract-testing.md)
for contract order, test-first slices and acceptance. Use the
[execution harness](../../core/execution-harness.md) for completion. Runtime and
language versions are owned by `global.json` and the affected project/build files.
Resolve the SDK separately from the target/runtime; check `api/Dockerfile`,
`api/Directory.Build.props` and both NuGet locks for provider compatibility.
Use [SDK selection guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/tools/global-json)
and official documentation matching the discovered framework/package release;
generic examples do not establish prerelease API availability.

Start at the affected controller or service and its existing tests. Follow
[shared investigation](../../core/context-loading.md#investigation) when the path
or cause is uncertain. Preserve the Controllers, Services, Dto, Models and Data
ownership boundaries; reuse existing registration and routing conventions.

Load specialist detail only for the selected decision:

| Work | Reference |
|---|---|
| Designing an interface, async flow or dependency lifetime | [Architecture](architecture-guidelines.md) |
| Choosing a test seam or replacing a dependency | [Testing and mocking](testing-and-mocking.md) |
| Changing an API contract, generated client or mocks | [OpenAPI procedure](../openapi-expert/SKILL.md) |
| Changing PostgreSQL SQL, EF mappings, indexes, migrations or persistence concurrency | [Database procedure](../database/SKILL.md) |

## Implementation and testing

Use existing xUnit tests under `api/src/RecipeApi.Tests/`. Run focused feedback with
`task test:api -- --filter <expression>`. Choose a unit test for isolated behavior;
use the existing `TestWebApplicationFactory` and database fixtures when acceptance
crosses those seams. Inspect the selected fixture's provider and replacements:
an in-memory provider cannot establish PostgreSQL constraints or relational behavior.
Preserve persisted workflow side effects that subsequent reads depend on.
For auth acceptance, select the auth-enabled factory; for worker execution or
startup wiring, inspect whether the selected fixture runs those production paths.

Keep file-scoped namespaces and existing implicit/explicit using conventions.
Use collection expressions where compatible with the target type and behavior.
Extend established controller routes and dependency injection; add an abstraction
only when the selected behavior needs it. Keep persistence conversions explicit.
Request validation, auth, JSON wrapping and error behavior follow the approved
operation and existing controller/middleware pipeline in `Program.cs`. Inspect
those seams and their tests before adopting a framework-default response or a
minimal-API example. Preserve existing HttpClient registration and secret handling;
keep credentials out of logs and test evidence.

Use targeted discovery or drift commands when their output answers a current
question. Static route/schema comparison does not establish live parity; the
shared verifier selects applicable final checks.
---
name: database
description: Change or review WFS PostgreSQL schema, migrations, EF mappings, queries, indexes and persistence concurrency. Use when PostgreSQL storage or provider behavior is in scope.
---

# Database and schema evolution

Follow [contract/testing](../../core/contract-testing.md) and the selected scope:
approved schema/API intent → regression tests → implementation. Persistence has
its own representation: API DTOs need not match tables, views, JSONB or workflow
rows one-to-one. Verify conversions, constraints, nullability and EF mappings in
`api/src/RecipeApi/Data/RecipeDbContext.cs` and the affected Models/Dto files.
Do not copy an API schema into storage or guess vector dimensions from examples.

`api/database/schema.sql` owns clean-install declarative DDL;
`api/database/compatibility.sql` handles existing-database transitions;
`api/database/migrate.sh` runs the migration sequence. Update all affected SQL,
EF mappings and tests, including backup/restore dependencies when applicable.
Use the repository's fluent EF configuration and existing mapping conventions.

## Select evidence and versions

Start with the affected requirement under `openspec/specs/`, then its regression
assertions and current SQL/service code. Search and indexing have separate owners;
backup/recovery distinguishes merge restore from exact replacement. Preserve their
qualifications rather than inferring guarantees from test names or code comments.

Resolve PostgreSQL/pgvector from the selected Compose files, migration tooling from
`api/database/Dockerfile`, and EF/Npgsql/Pgvector.NET from the affected `.csproj`,
`api/Directory.Build.props` and `packages.lock.json` files. Image tags and locks
declare inputs; they do not establish installed extensions or running versions.
Use matching [PostgreSQL manuals](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/),
[Npgsql provider documentation](https://www.npgsql.org/efcore/) and
[pgvector release documentation](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector#readme).
Check the selected package/release metadata before adopting a current-doc example.

Load only the evidence relevant to the selected persistence decision:

| Decision | Existing evidence to inspect |
|---|---|
| Schema transitions and constraints | `SchemaIntegrityTests.cs` (static/model assertions) and `NonCookingPostgresTests.cs`, `RecipeImportReportPostgresTests.cs` (database assertions) |
| Search SQL, filtering, vectors or plans | `recipe-search` and `search-indexing` specs; `RecipeLexicalSearchPostgresTests.cs` and `RecipeSearchFilterMaterializerPostgresTests.cs` |
| Concurrent grocery writes | `grocery-shopping` spec; `GroceryCheckConcurrencyPostgresTests*.cs`; `GroceryCheckCoordinator.cs` for the single-instance processing boundary |
| Backup/restore dependencies | `data-backup-and-recovery` spec; `OnlineRecoveryPostgresTests.cs` and the affected merge/sidecar tests |

Tests above live under `api/src/RecipeApi.Tests/Integration/`; service owners live
under `api/src/RecipeApi/Services/`. For query work, inspect parameter binding,
provider translation and index/operator compatibility in the actual execution path.
The existing search repositories use bound `NpgsqlParameter` values. Do not infer
plan use or recall from an index declaration. PostgreSQL-specific transactions,
isolation and lock effects belong here; .NET scope/cancellation/disposal belong to
[dotnet-dev](../dotnet-dev/SKILL.md).

## Preview and application

Run from the repository root after verifying the target database, Compose inputs
and authorized effects. Inspect generated SQL before applying it.

| Operation | Command | Coverage / effect |
|---|---|---|
| Schema preview | `task db:schema:push DRY_RUN=true` | psqldef dry-run of schema.sql only; does not preview compatibility.sql |
| Apply migration | `task migrate` | Compose migration sidecar, including compatibility SQL; changes the configured DB |
| Start database | `task dev:db` | Starts configured PostgreSQL service |
| Database shell | `task shell:db` | Interactive access to configured DB |
| Export schema | `task db:schema:pull` | Overwrites schema.sql from live DB; inspect and preserve local edits first |

Review compatibility SQL separately; schema-only preview cannot establish safety
of the full migration. Declarative tooling can still produce destructive changes.
Inspect `migrate.sh` end to end: extension and concurrent-index presteps run before
the compatibility transaction, followed by psqldef. The full sequence is not atomic.
For affected populated tables, review lock scope/duration, partial completion and
retry behavior. Preserve concurrent-index work outside transaction blocks and its
invalid-index recovery; consult the selected PostgreSQL major's `CREATE INDEX`
and explicit-locking documentation. Plan experiments belong in authorized isolated
fixtures; `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` executes the query and is not a read-only preview.

Schema application must never silently reset data. Reset, DROP, truncate, volume
removal, reseeding or restore require explicit authorization covering the data and
environment; routine schema authorization does not imply them. Never substitute
`task dev:clean:sync` for schema apply: it removes volumes and images. No implicit
fallback to reset when migration fails. Report the failure and continue only safe,
authorized work. Do not overwrite approved DDL to match incidental live drift.

Verify clean-install and existing-data paths when applicable. Assert persisted
rows and constraints as well as API behavior. In-memory tests and static SQL/EF
comparison do not establish live PostgreSQL parity. Record unavailable DB checks
as blocked. Select PostgreSQL feedback through the shared
[database runner guidance](../../core/execution-harness.md#effects-blockers-and-supporting-commands),
including `task test:database`; its prerequisites, effects and completion checks
remain owned there. Reading a fixture or a static assertion is not a passing run.

A whole-use and partial-use double declaration in one exhaustive group is contradictory.

All semantic edits advance contentRevision. Unrelated bindings may be revalidated/carried to the new revision only when their ingredient facts, textRevision, source evidence and dependency graph are unchanged. Deleted rows/steps or changed text invalidate affected bindings and downstream remainders. Do not silently relink a duplicated word or ID. Approved ingredient-total edit policy: preserve explicit absolute allocations at their saved original values, retain relative fractions of the corrected total and update proven whole uses. The absolute amount continues to scale with portions; changing a total must not silently redistribute it. Revalidate allocation groups and downstream remainders; inconsistencies retain readable wording and quiet review without blocking cooking.

The first ordinary whole-use producer uses the existing binding payload extension
for `{relationshipEvidence:{version:1,rule:"explicit-whole-clause",sourceRevision,
originalAmount}}`. This internal marker grants no trust: fresh publication rederives
proof against source-aligned canonical originals, and edit carry requires the guarded
previous snapshot. Public binding/DTO shapes and generated-client consumers remain
unchanged. Empty pre-upgrade staged bindings remain a valid quiet fallback. The
[step design](../scale-cooking-step-ingredients/design.md#slice-1-evidence-inlet)
owns bounded grammar and dependency validation; other roles retain existing payloads.

## Grocery rows and check mutations

Recipe grocery row: `{rowId, rowVersion, weekStartDate, source:"recipe", demandIdentity, quantity, unitText, quantityComplete, recipeIds, displayName, section}`. `quantity` uses the exact scalar/range union; known incomplete subtotal is explicit. Names are labels. demandIdentity binds saved food ID or conservative fallback identity, purchase qualifiers and compatible unit bucket. Stable server rowId persists for proven continuing demand; no rowId comes from localized text. Exact demand-identity matches continue directly. For an unmatched unit-bucket change, a unique one-to-one contributor lineage (same saved ingredient rows and scheduled occurrence IDs, same food/purchase meaning, no competing split/merge) can prove row continuity even when quantity comparison is impossible. This preserves the check for an incompatible-unit change without claiming equivalence. Ambiguous lineage does not establish continuation. Retired identities never revive a stale checked row. New split/merge/semantically changed groups get new IDs and start unchecked (no inference of shopping acknowledgement); continuing rows follow proven increase policy. Alex approved this structural policy: new split/merge rows start unchecked; unchanged continuing rows retain checks unless their checked-demand baseline proves an increase. At upgrade there is no active recipe-derived list to transfer; the next list starts new without deleting historical records.

Existing PATCH `/api/schedule/{weekOffset}/grocery/item` is proposed to require `{rowId,weekStartDate,expectedRowVersion,checked,clientMutationId}`. Preserve captured reference Monday and verify offset resolves the same absolute week. Success becomes 200 `{updatedAt,weekStartDate,rowId,rowVersion,checked}`; 409 stale/missing row/version returns current row or absent marker without applying the stale intention. Unknown row never creates a phantom. Repeat clientMutationId+identical body returns its saved outcome without applying again; changed body under same ID conflicts. Serialise same-row optimistic intents; apply only matching equal/newer version responses. A lost reply requires reread before replay. Extras keep existing occurrence endpoint/version and actual occurrence week even when presented in future shopping views.

Existing bulk grocery PATCH remains an explicit guarded replacement: proposed `{weekStartDate,expectedListVersion,checks:{rowId:boolean}}`, response 200 `{data:{weekStartDate,listVersion,checks}}`. Missing keys clear only in the matching list version, not from stale name dictionaries. Name-only writes return 409 upgrade_required after cutover. Item changes on unrelated rows need not conflict from unrelated checks; recompute changes affected rowVersion when comparison/check state changes. Existing `grocery_updated` and schedule DTOs must carry absolute week/list/row versions and row checks together; late old snapshots cannot restore newer state. Proposed recipe rowVersion/listVersion are monotonically increasing unsigned-64 decimal strings (initial 1, compared exactly, never JS floating-point). Every committed check mutation, guarded bulk replacement or changed recompute advances listVersion; affected rows advance rowVersion. Unchanged retries are no-ops and return saved versions. Thus a stale bulk baseline cannot erase an intervening item check, while item writes on different current rows need not conflict. Locale-only label changes do not reset identities/checks. ContentRevision remains opaque: recipe clients reject stale reads using request/context generation and captured token, not lexical ordering. Demo generation/recovery gates remain, and the initially supported single application instance must remain explicit; multi-replica durability is not established by in-process locks.

Approved comparison uses the **checked-demand baseline**, not the previous recomputation. A successful unchecked→checked transition captures the current exact requirement, completeness, unit definition/bucket and demand identity at that same coordinated commit. Persist server-owned `checkedDemandBaseline` as null when unchecked or `{quantity, quantityComplete, unit, demandIdentity, acknowledgedAtRowVersion}` when checked, captured from authoritative current row demand at the transition. Quantity uses the same exact scalar/range/null union; unit retains the evidenced conversion definition. Include this baseline and its association in current-format recovery without a new acknowledgement control. A scalar is the degenerate interval [q,q]. Convert compatible units exactly; a complete comparable current requirement proves increase only when current.min > baseline.max. Alex approved baseline 2–3 → current 3–4 staying checked and → current 4–5 unchecking.

While the row remains checked, equivalent, decreased, overlapping, unknown or incomparable updates preserve **both** its check and its original baseline. They never ratchet that baseline forward. Thus checked 2–3 → 3–4 → 4–5 still compares 4 to the original maximum 3 and resets, even if each adjacent update overlaps. A smaller interim requirement also does not lower the baseline. Unknown/incomplete baselines cannot prove a later increase and must not silently become known merely because current demand becomes complete. Unit changes without exact comparison remain unprovable even if row continuity is established.

An unchecked→checked transition after a genuine uncheck captures a fresh baseline. A redundant checked=true, identical mutation retry, full-map entry that remains true, response replay, read or unchanged recomputation preserves the existing baseline; only false→true creates a new one. Explicit or automatic uncheck clears the active baseline, and new/split/merged rows start unchecked without inheriting predecessors’ baselines. Full-map replacement captures baselines only for false→true entries, retains existing true baselines and clears omitted/false ones. Proven increase atomically unchecks the affected row once and increments row/list versions; after the shopper checks the new amount, unchanged recomputation preserves that later check/baseline. Do not reconstruct a missing/corrupt baseline from current demand as if it were acknowledged; retain an honest unknown comparison state and report integrity errors through existing diagnostics.

Keep completeness distinct from check intent. No `checkReviewReason`, prior-unknown acknowledgement or replacement badge. Existing one brief list-level increase explanation may remain once per actual reset, never on mere read or uncertainty.

## Food identity and category correction

**Deferred bilingual release, not a portions prerequisite:** `FoodIdentity {id,revision,labels:{en,fr},aliases:[{locale,text,matchKey,relation:"exact",sourceRef,reviewedAt}],qualifiers,status}`; only validated labels publish, otherwise retain source shopping name. External IDs remain provenance, never primary key. A saved mapping records dictionary version, evidence, origin and human-protected fields. Household correction affects that household/recipe association, never automatically a global alias. Conflicting exact aliases are unresolved; broad/related/nutrient group relationships cannot merge foods.

Before bilingual cutover normal category PATCH `/api/ingredients/{key}/category` retains its normalized-key scope. Afterward propose explicit `/api/foods/{foodId}/category` for validated household food overrides; unresolved rows keep their fallback-key scope. Required `{grocerySection,expectedCategoryRevision}` → 204 only after existing persistence/recompute contract; 409 stale correction; no mutation of extra occurrences. Category migration conflicts retain each prior human choice and unresolved rows instead of selecting the last write. Extras retain their occurrence PATCH. UI control parity never implies endpoint/scope parity.

## Formats

Proposed recipe envelope `format:"wfs-recipe",version:2,recipeId,contentSchemaVersion:2,contentRevision,content,...`; full snapshot manifest `format:"wfs-snapshot",version:2,schemaFingerprint,householdId,artifacts,hashes`. Include every identity/dictionary reference and household override actually persisted and required to reproduce meaning; an absent optional catalogue is not a missing baseline artifact. Preserve exact quantities/notation, units/packages, source/protection, sections/bindings, prepared/serving state, row/check versions, media and durable obligations. Reject unsupported old formats in ordinary restore before any mutation. One-time forward importer has explicit accepted source formats and a separate manifest; it is not routine restore. Current-format ordinary merge uses an explicitly captured destination contentRevision/content hash in its reviewed import manifest, plus field protection. Identical content is a no-op; absent destination IDs can be staged under that operation’s membership rules. Nonidentical existing content requires a matching captured destination baseline and approved field selection; stale, missing or divergent baselines defer. No full historical revision ledger or timestamp ordering is assumed. Exact restore is an explicitly selected replacement with complete relationship/media preflight. Opaque tokens cannot be ordered by timestamps.

# Design

## Current delivery checkpoint

At `a666a64f`, canonical storage/guarded editing, flagged correction and fresh
URL/photo publication have bounded local evidence. See [tasks](tasks.md) for exact
records and remaining criteria. Ordinary binding production is not implemented;
it now includes import and post-edit reevaluation under the step companion.
The [accepted baseline](proposal.md) sets coordinated deployment, maintenance reuse,
old-client refresh and bilingual deferral. The source descriptions below explicitly
refer to their historical checkpoints; do not reimplement them without checking
current code and evidence.

## Context and Existing Ownership

Source inspection at `d51222ffbb7e3eb6d08fed394851a52de3f5522c`, branch `recipe-view-redesign`, 2026-11-07. Uncommitted browser-parity edits are concurrent evidence, not part of this change. `RecipeService.UpdateRecipe` writes string Ingredients while `SupperIngredientProjection.Read` requires whole-list coherence before binding retained supply. Its `IntentionallyUnquantified` phrase list is not a validity rule for the new model. `CategorizeIngredientsProcessor` still reads raw supply. `SyncRecipeProcessor` replaces raw content and basis from disk. These were competing publication paths at that historical checkpoint; current URL/photo and guarded editing support is recorded above.

The existing projection/context and durable invalidation owners remain authoritative for dated counts, previews, cooked baseline and prepared receipts. The new model replaces their recipe input. Shared ownership and conflicts are in [review.md](review.md), exact proposed public/persistence boundaries in [contracts.md](contracts.md).

## Decisions and Tradeoffs

Use one `contentRevision` instead of the old draft's `ingredientRevision`: ingredients, basis, step text/bindings and shopping association can invalidate one another. This increases honest conflicts between simultaneous editors, but prevents mixed revisions. Notes/rating-only updates remain independent. Stable IDs are unrelated to order, displayed name and food ID.

Use bounded exact rational quantities, a tagged scalar/range union, independently nullable unit, original notation and explicit scaling policy. A stored zero is real, missing is unknown. Strings are rendered compatibility output; no second quantity store or prose parser on reads. Preserve source evidence/provenance separately. No whitelist of qualitative phrases and no always-visible repair selectors.

A complete content read includes all instructions and original facts even where step bindings are uncertain. Safe migration may retain a per-recipe legacy adapter until canonical publication can preserve trustworthy facts and exact wording. Never zip by position or import rounded projections. A known 200 g with unknown basis remains known original 200 g.

Import-time AI may propose facts and identities through existing provider boundaries. It cannot certify evidence or publish over protected human values. Existing Report issue/Review issue plus eligible reimport remain available. `RecipeAgent` currently writes recipe.json before `SyncRecipeProcessor` updates the DB; unchanged reuse would bypass protection. Future controlled reprocessing must stage results before file and DB publication, compare captured content/source revisions and preserve unselected media and human edits. Report state is not ingredient completeness and generation is not a saved correction.

## First Observable Slice

The approved sequence now extracts the coherent identity/guarded-publication
prerequisite needed by grocery continuity before grocery closure. See the
[prerequisite review](grocery-prerequisite-review.md) for boundaries, recovery
activation gate, precision proof limits and required checks. This does not close
this change or its companions and does not narrow grocery acceptance.

Search → detail at eight portions from basis four → Edit original 200 g pasta and untouched 100 ml sauce → Save pasta 250 g → reread 250 g original and 500 g dated, with one shared revision and source retained. Include a proven whole-use step in the coordinated step slice; until that slice passes, this tracer is not complete portions support. Exercise UI → generated client → real API → PostgreSQL plus durable grocery/search invalidation, and method-sensitive mock equivalents.

## State, Concurrency and Recovery

A guarded write atomically changes original facts, dependent-binding validity, human protection, contentRevision and durable derived obligations. Derived execution and notification remain later effects with updating/failed/current status. A timeout may follow commit: preserve the draft, reread and reconcile, never blindly replay. Concurrent ingredient/step writers using one baseline cannot both succeed.

Explicit nulls/empty collections are authoritative; retained metadata cannot revive them. Unrelated IDs/order/sections/media stay unchanged. A local active cooking session retains its coherent installed revision until explicit accepted refresh; a new read of a prepared meal uses current recipe with recorded prepared portions, never a fabricated historical snapshot.

## Compatibility, Rollout and Reversal

Alex confirms that frontend, backend and database deploy together as one release.
Do not design a rolling mixed-version backend/schema compatibility period or a
permanent legacy string-write adapter. Canonical records reject old ingredient/
instruction payloads atomically even with a current revision; stale tabs use the
supported refresh route with recoverable drafts and current-original reconciliation.
The current app's unconverted/review-material editing path remains supported.
Coordinated deployment still requires guarding delayed workers, preserving data
and verifying the matching application/schema recovery pair.

Add storage, settle contracts and client/draft fencing, qualify guarded publication, then in-place conversion under [rollout.md](rollout.md). Recovery and current-format-only support belong to the migration companion. No permanent legacy backup adapters. A per-recipe legacy read adapter during conversion is not old-backup restore compatibility. Disabling new code after new writes is not safe rollback.

## User Experience

Keep amount, unit and description as the primary editor fields. Accept fractions/ranges in amount. Shopping-name correction and fixed exceptions use progressive disclosure. Original and Reset stay in recipe actions; preserve quiet preview state, current phone/tablet composition, horizontal portions editor, original overlays, drafts, check states, exact offset and completion protections. Review EN/FR at 320 CSS px, 200% text and tablet Split View separately from automated checks.

## Approved decisions and remaining qualification

Alex approved keeping an explicit partial step amount at its original value when the ingredient total changes; it still scales with portions. Relative language stays relative to the corrected total. Proven whole uses…1441 tokens truncated…th no trustworthy measurement is valid canonical text with independently absent amount/unit. Alex approved retaining usable ingredient/step wording from a fresh intake whose trustworthy facts cannot safely become canonical. The retained material is a guarded publication into the existing unready editable recipe, with original source and an operation receipt that says review material was retained, not that extraction completed. The extraction task remains failed and the existing content-review flag exposes it. No legacy-only publication is marked successful or ready; malformed or contradictory proposals cannot become validated facts merely to finish the workflow.

Recovery uses the existing Ready for review filter and original-content editor. A person can correct ingredients and steps, Save and reopen; an eligible changed Ingredients/Steps comment with a usable URL starts the existing guarded repair. An unchanged comment does nothing. Neither manual Save nor flag resolution certifies full import. For the witnessed fresh-URL review path, the accepted repair's captured human content becomes the candidate. Its retained supply must uniquely associate with the corrected line, and the current human text must have a losslessly representable exact amount/unit/description. An explicit human change from `200 g pasta, diced` to `250 g pasta` therefore supplies 250 g canonical facts while the earlier 200 g supply token remains separately retained as source evidence. Ambiguous associations or unrepresentable wording fail the attempt and leave the recipe editable and unready; no quantity is guessed from prose. Success publishes `review-canonical` under that repair task's journal with human-protected ingredient facts and fresh stable IDs, then existing hero/sync/category/readiness/report tasks can complete. The original failed extraction receipt never changes. A retry resumes committed delivery without calling the provider again, and a late replay cannot replace newer human fields. This narrow path does not turn older legacy reports or a manual Save into canonical repairs; general existing-recipe reprocessing remains task 3.1 work.

A human edit, clear, source replacement or membership change after capture rejects the delayed operation before any partial overwrite. After commit, interrupted delivery resumes the retained output without another provider call; a late completed replay must not reinstall old files over a newer edit. A report remains a report: no automatic unrelated resolution or correction claim. Existing household/history/extras are outside the selected write set.

### Binding boundary and remaining dependency

This milestone deliberately leaves new bindings empty/uncertain. `CookingStepProjection.Valid` verifies structural/revision/span/arithmetic conditions for already-confirmed uses; a provider-supplied `whole` label or `status=validated` cannot establish exhaustive semantic use. Matching a quantity to the row total, name or position is insufficient. A later narrowly reviewed inlet must specify what immutable evidence certifies ingredient association and whole/partial intent, validate unique UTF-16 spans and numeric roles, and abstain on ambiguous/repeated/time/temperature/package numbers. No new binding editor, language ontology or global inference rule is introduced here. Existing seeded-binding engine/live tests remain evidence for projection, not ordinary binding production.

### Acceptance and smallest alternatives

Use an existing CanonicalIngredientPublicationPostgresTests partial with the actual bootstrap/URL workflow and external-provider doubles. Prove fresh publication through ready status, ordinary generated-client edit/read/projection and grocery recompute; stable ingredient/step IDs, exact fractions/ranges/zero/null basis, source/media retention, no duplicate demand, and no household/history/extra changes. Include qualitative text and an unrepresentable trustworthy candidate, caller-forged freshness, delayed human clear, malformed IDs/operands, precommit cancellation, commit-before-delivery failure, unchanged retry, late replay after a later edit, and ordinary current-format backup/seed read-back of the new receipt/facts. Existing receipt/guard tests stay intact. Configure/discover the resulting native owner in the real PostgreSQL CI job and explicitly qualify a focused real browser/client seam; a mocked or seeded-content pass cannot establish the intake path.

The smallest coherent approach extends the existing transaction/journal and current codec. Converting after SyncRecipe is fewer call-site lines but breaks the single producer receipt/commit boundary and complicates replay. Making all old canonical writers pass is smaller syntactically but grants unqualified overwrite authority. A broader typed repair/binding-proposal pipeline could eventually serve more channels, but requires saved-identity/protection and semantic-proof decisions not settled by this first milestone. Guarded canonical success and distinct unready review retention serve different outcomes; neither claims complete step scaling or existing-recipe repair.

### Approved original-photo intake extension (2026-11-11)

Alex approved extending the same guarded canonical/review publication to **new photo recipes only** when the original photo and empty destination are verified. `recipe-import` also serves PDF and existing-recipe repairs, so its name or image presence alone grants no freshness. The extraction must descend from the original delivered photo bootstrap under the *same captured follow-up workflow ID*, with its declared original image bytes selected in the launch, no `original/source.pdf`, no HTML source, no prior ingredient/raw/canonical content and no ready state. Validate the retained follow-up intent and exact launch/field/file ancestry before publication. A later `recipe-import` on the same photo recipe cannot borrow that bootstrap. PDF-rendered pages cannot qualify as original photos.

Lossless photo extraction publishes `fresh-canonical` through the existing journal, hero, sync and readiness owners without replacing source images. Usable but unsafe wording publishes distinct unready `review-material` and the existing failed-extraction flag. A human can edit ingredient and step wording, then submit a changed eligible Ingredients/Steps comment; the existing image-backed `recipe-import` repair intent must capture those saved fields. Only that guarded repair may publish `review-canonical` from the selected human wording, without another provider response, then complete readiness/report flow. Manual Save/Resolve is not completion. Preserve failed receipts, replay protection, source/media bytes and unrelated human edits. General reimport, PDF, synthesis and share remain separate task 3.1 channels.

## Approved flagged-correction slice (2026-11-10)

The strict automated publication proposal above must not make a person's recipe read-only. Reuse RecipeImportReport, its reported/reviewed states, existing Reported search filter and badge; introduce no new draft status or product workflow. Only an exhausted semantic ingredient/usable-step validation failure with retained recipe content can create a missing system flag. Select only the failed content reasons, use Ready for review and its generic explanation, and persist a short safe explanation in the existing comment field. Acquisition, provider transport, image and category failures keep existing failed-capture handling. Preserve existing reports and only associate ordinary repair-failure diagnostics with their matching attempt. No automatic report resolution, repair launch or Ready transition follows a manual save.

The explicit filter-only report/review queue includes flagged unready recipes. Typed lexical/vector search and normal discovery/planning remain ready-only; do not infer expanded search eligibility from review-queue access. Detail and PATCH already support unready records. Open/Edit initializes authoritative original content, even when the dated projection cannot be read; it never saves a scaled preview as originals. The same editor offers original steps, stable canonical section/step IDs, and the existing legacy instruction representation without conversion on ordinary Save. Add/remove retains all unaffected wording and identities. Save, Cancel, error recovery and conflict reconciliation include steps as well as ingredients. Local unsaved edit recovery is an existing technical facility, not a new recipe status.

Canonical Save keeps human provenance/protection, independently nullable quantity/unit and original text. A changed step or invalidated ingredient dependency makes only unsafe proof ineligible for projection; unrelated valid uses remain usable. Do not guess allocations, erase readable instructions, or require a binding editor. Revision conflicts preserve the person's unsaved changes and require the existing intentional reread/reconciliation; automation captured earlier cannot overwrite an accepted correction.

Acceptance follows semantic content failure with retained material → existing Ready for review filter → open/Edit original ingredients and steps → Save/reopen → delayed producer rejection. Cover canonical and legacy content, no safe bindings, empty instructions, blank amount/unit, dated projection failure, Cancel/failure/reconciliation, unchanged report membership and unrelated household/history/extras. Use real normal-app/API/PostgreSQL and a generated-client/browser seam, plus CI discovery and final scoped verification. No whole-spec completion from this increment.

Existing flag comments keep their established meaning: a nonblank note on an eligible content report may request automated repair; a flag without a note is for human review. A system explanation SHALL describe the content issue without raw diagnostics, overwriting existing comments, or launching repair. Existing commented reports retain their guarded repair behavior and complete authorship/history/state.

## Reviewed system-review refinement (2026-11-10)

Alex approved a system flag only for actual ingredient/usable-step validation needs on retained editable recipe content. Use the existing Ready for review status and generic explanation, with a short system-authored explanatory comment and no repair launch. Unchanged feedback Save is a no-op; a changed human comment keeps the existing eligible correction rules (source URL/images, Ingredients/Steps, no Duplicate), history and stale-write protection. Do not turn image/category/transport failures into content reports or overwrite existing feedback. This is a limited bridge from content validation to the existing review queue, not replacement of failed-capture management. Review wording must not claim a re-import happened. Resolve retains its existing feedback-only semantics.

Use the existing Clear/deferred-cleanup guard conservatively: persisted ingredient/instruction/canonical content, including explicit empty saved collections, survives. This also retains some partial automated content; the trade-off avoids a new human-ownership marker/schema or recovery mechanism. Empty placeholders remain eligible for existing cleanup. Preserve the original-step editor and original-content entry, and verify system review → manual correction → reopen → changed comment correction, no-op unchanged save (including after backup/read-back), report preservation, clear protection and stale-job safety. The earlier broad failure-flag proposal is superseded; URL/photo canonical source publication is locally qualified, while other intake channels and ordinary binding production remain unfinished. Broader tasks and archive stay open until required acceptance passes.

The classifier does not treat arbitrary partial provider output as a completed extraction. For witnessed fresh URL work, the extractor may publish usable normalized wording as `review-material` under the existing journal before raising the typed semantic-content failure. The worker passes that classification after exhausting the attempt. The report owner verifies the persisted failed ExtractRecipe task and retained recipe before inserting a flag. Provider/network/image/category errors do not share that signal. Empty acquisition placeholders remain in existing failed-capture management.

The system explanation is stored in the existing report note, not dropped or hidden behind generic copy. No new origin field/status is needed: unchanged feedback without a retained RepairIntentId is a no-op, independently of authorship; an existing retained command keeps its original retry/reconciliation path. A changed comment or other eligible changed feedback requests a newly captured correction under existing rules. Current backup/read-back already preserves note/reasons/status and absence of a repair command; qualify that unchanged restored feedback cannot create one. Missing/deleted member attribution is never used to infer system origin.

# Network topology reference

## Browser and server URLs are different

[config.ts](../../pwa/src/lib/constants/config.ts) and the
[Kiota adapter](../../pwa/src/lib/api/api-client.ts) default the browser API base to
an empty string. [useScheduleStream](../../pwa/src/hooks/useScheduleStream.ts) builds
`/api/stream` when that base is empty and uses credentials. Same-origin browser
requests behind Traefik retain `/api`; do not expose Docker service names to browsers.
Do not require a literal `/` base: callers concatenate paths, and a leading `/` base
can produce `//api/...`. Inspect each affected URL builder when changing the base.

[serverFetch](../../pwa/src/lib/api/server-client.ts) concatenates `API_INTERNAL_URL`
and the endpoint without normalization. Its default and the production override use
`http://api:9001`, the configured absolute container-network URL. It explicitly forwards
`h_access` in the Cookie header and identity as `X-Family-Member-Id`. This internal
request does not change the browser origin. The retired claim that both bases must
be `/`, or that internal absolute URLs inherently break SSR cookies, was incorrect.

## Configuration owners

- [apps.yml](../../docker/compose/apps.yml) defines API `/api` routing, the dedicated
  priority-100 stream router and `sse-headers@file` middleware. The prefix is retained.
  [traefik_dynamic.yml](../../docker/compose/traefik_dynamic.yml) defines the headers
  and additional local-host routes; inspect the composed configuration for deployment.
- [production-overrides.yml](../../docker/compose/production-overrides.yml) binds the
  host `DATA_ROOT` location to `/data`; the base API sets container `DATA_ROOT=/data`.
  [production.yml](../../docker/compose/production.yml) separately overrides container
  `DATA_ROOT` with the host variable. Do not assume those different compositions
  produce the same storage path. Verify rendered env and mounts before deployment.
- Both production files default Traefik host ports to 9100 (HTTP) and 9180 (admin),
  with overrides. These are legacy configuration facts, not public-release requirements.
  Current public installation and qualification guidance lives in
  [release-template/synology/README.md](../../release-template/synology/README.md).
- `DOMAIN_NAME` is a host routing value, not a URL with scheme/path.
  [auth.ts](../../pwa/src/lib/auth.ts) and
  [identity cookies](../../pwa/src/lib/identity/cookie.ts) read optional
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_COOKIE_DOMAIN`. A parent domain is not universally required.
